questions.q: What is the correct SOQL syntax to pull a Contact's parent Account name alongside the Contact's own Name?
options: SELECT Contact.Name, Account.Name FROM Account.Contact
SELECT Name, Account.Name FROM Contact
SELECT Name, (SELECT Name FROM Account) FROM Contact
SELECT Name, Account FROM Contact JOIN Account
questions.explain: Child-to-parent queries use simple dot notation — Account.Name — directly in the SELECT list, no subquery needed.

questions.q: Why doesn't a child-to-parent query need a nested subquery the way a parent-to-child query does?
options: Child-to-parent queries actually do require a subquery, just a shorter one
Parent objects never have more than one field
SOQL simply doesn't support subqueries in the child-to-parent direction
Every child record has exactly one parent via its lookup/master-detail field, so there's no list to nest — the parent's fields just become more fields on the same row
questions.explain: One Account can have many Contacts (needs nesting), but one Contact has only one Account — nothing to nest, so dot notation flattens it into the same row.

questions.q: Can a dot-notation field like Account.Industry be used in a WHERE clause?
options: No — dot notation only works in the SELECT list
Only in parent-to-child subqueries
Only if the field is first aliased
Yes — SELECT Name FROM Contact WHERE Account.Industry = 'Technology' is valid
questions.explain: Dot notation works in WHERE just as it does in SELECT, letting you filter child records by a field that lives on the parent object.

questions.q: For a custom lookup field literally named Account__c on a custom object, what's the relationship name used to traverse to the parent's fields?
options: Account__c
Account__r
Account_Parent
Account__rel
questions.explain: __c stores the relationship (the field itself); __r is the relationship name used to traverse to the parent object's fields.

questions.q: Structurally, what's the key difference between a parent-to-child query and a child-to-parent query?
options: Child-to-parent requires a JOIN keyword while parent-to-child does not
Parent-to-child only works on custom objects
There is no structural difference between the two
Parent-to-child nests a nested subquery in the SELECT list because one parent can have many children; child-to-parent uses flat dot notation because one child has exactly one parent
questions.explain: The cardinality difference (many children vs. one parent) is exactly why one direction needs a subquery and the other doesn't.
